correctness.rationale: For binary circular words excluding cyclic 000 and 111, the ten permitted four-grams are arcs of a six-vertex de Bruijn digraph. A profile is realizable exactly when its nonnegative integral circulation has connected positive support. Solving the five independent balance variables gives B(z)=(1+z^6)/[(1-z^2)(1-z^3)^2(1-z^4)(1-z^6)]. The six simple directed cycles have exactly two vertex-disjoint pairs; their positive union contributions are z^6/(1-z^3)^2 and z^6/[(1-z^2)(1-z^4)], yielding C(z) after subtraction of zero. Nonzero genuine poles at the necessary roots imply least quasi-period twelve; pole at 1 gives n^4/5184. Fresh independent direct enumeration compared profile sets and generating-function coefficients for n=1..17.
residual_risks: The independent literal enumeration was finite through n=17; infinite theorem rests on exact cycle decomposition and GF derivation.

evidence: General theorem: if restricted de Bruijn graph strongly connected, profile counts quasipolynomials of degree |E|-|V| and period dividing lcm simple cycle lengths. Here |E|-|V|=4, lcm=12, but exact coefficient and least period require additional calculation.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general theorem gives degree <=4 and period divisor 12 but does not determine complete coefficients, exact least period, or subtraction of disconnected supports. Thus the explicit rational C(z) is not a known automatic numerical corollary.
